title: Newsdesk story: three civic works
lede: A short three-story flight from Curitiba's 1974 bus corridors to Medellín's Metro and New York's High Line, cited from official city pages. Pins are approximate.
cta: Open in GlobeDesk and browse the rundown, or press Play to fly the stories in order.

stories.title: Curitiba's BRT corridors, opened in 1974
stories.summary: The City of Curitiba, marking 50 years of its bus rapid transit system in 2024, says the system was inaugurated on 22 September 1974 on the North/South axis, beginning with 20 kilometres of exclusive bus corridors.

stories.script: The City of Curitiba, in an official 2024 notice marking 50 years of its bus rapid transit system, says the system was inaugurated on 22 September 1974 on the North/South axis, beginning with 20 kilometres of exclusive bus corridors. The pin is approximate.

captions.text: Inaugurated on 22 September 1974, the city says.

cards.title: Curitiba BRT
cards.body: An official City of Curitiba news notice dated 28 November 2024, marking 50 years of the city's BRT, says the system was inaugurated by then mayor Jaime Lerner on 22 September 1974 on the North/South axis, and began with 20 kilometres of exclusive corridors for high-capacity buses, called canaletas. The same notice says the corridors carry 65 percent of the passengers of Curitiba's collective transport, as stated in that 2024 article. Later performance and fleet figures in the article are not copied here.
cards.why: An official city account of a transit model that other cities later adopted.

stories.title: Medellín's Metro and the first Metrocable line
stories.summary: Metro de Medellín's official history says the company was created on 31 May 1979 and began commercial train service on 30 November 1995. Línea K, the north-eastern Metrocable, entered service on 7 August 2004.

location.name: Medellín Metro, Aburrá Valley (approx.)
location.note: Approximate city pin for Medellín / the Aburrá Valley system described by Metro de Medellín. The network spans several municipalities. A surveyed station coordinate is [UNKNOWN] in this card. Not a street address.

stories.script: Metro de Medellín's official history says the company was created on 31 May 1979 and began commercial service at 11 in the morning on 30 November 1995, on a first stretch of Línea A. The north-eastern Metrocable, Línea K, entered service on 7 August 2004. The pin is approximate.

captions.text: Trains from 1995; Metrocable Línea K from 7 August 2004.

cards.title: Metro de Medellín
cards.body: The official Metro de Medellín history page says the Empresa de Transporte Masivo del Valle de Aburrá was created on 31 May 1979, and that commercial operation began at 11:00 a.m. on 30 November 1995 on a first stretch of Línea A between Niquía and Poblado. It says Línea K, the north-eastern Metrocable, entered service on 7 August 2004, and that a second Metrocable, Línea J, began service on 3 March 2008. The same page later lists further cable, tram and bus lines. This card uses those dated opening facts and does not repeat later ridership totals.
cards.why: An official city-region transit history, including a mapped aerial cable line.

facts.label: Commercial service
facts.value: Began 30 November 1995, 11:00 a.m., Línea A between Niquía and Poblado.

stories.title: New York's High Line, first opened in 2009
stories.summary: NYC Parks says the West Side Elevated Line was fully operational by 1934, ceased operation in 1980, and that the first phase of the new park, from Gansevoort Street to West 20th Street, opened in June 2009.

location.name: The High Line, Manhattan (approx.)
location.note: Approximate pin for the High Line's first section in the Meatpacking District / Chelsea. Distinct from the Midtown Manhattan sample-practice pin and from UN Headquarters on the East River. A surveyed entrance coordinate is [UNKNOWN] in this card. Friends of the High Line states that section 1 opened on 8 June 2009.

stories.script: NYC Parks says the West Side Elevated Line was fully operational by 1934 and ceased operation in 1980. The first phase of the new park, from Gansevoort Street to West 20th Street, opened in June 2009. Friends of the High Line states that section 1 opened on 8 June 2009. The pin is approximate.

captions.text: The first park section opened in June 2009.

cards.title: The High Line
cards.body: The official NYC Parks historical sign for the High Line says the West Side Elevated Line, later known as the High Line, stretched from West 34th Street to a Spring Street terminal and was fully operational by 1934, then ceased operation in 1980. Friends of the High Line formed in 1999 to convert the abandoned structure to a public park. The first phase of the new park, from Gansevoort to West 20th Street, opened in June 2009; when fully opened by 2019, the park wrapped around Hudson Yards to West 34th Street. Friends of the High Line, the park conservancy, states that section 1 opened on 8 June 2009. A City of New York Parks Daily Plant article at a parks site URL was not successfully read and is not used as a source.
cards.why: An official city account of an elevated freight line turned into a public park.

facts.label: Freight line
facts.value: Fully operational by 1934; ceased operation in 1980 (NYC Parks).

facts.label: First park section

facts.label: Later extent
facts.value: Fully opened by 2019, wrapping around Hudson Yards to West 34th Street.
